claims.text: HfNbTaTiZr contains a heterogeneous microstructure of coherent nanoprecipitates embedded in a disordered matrix.
The nanoprecipitates and matrix have different thermal expansion coefficients.
Thermal-expansion mismatch at nanoprecipitate–matrix interfaces generates local stress fields.
Cooling from high-temperature processing produces residual stresses through thermal-expansion mismatch.
Rapid quenching retains a higher level of thermal-mismatch residual stress than sub-recrystallization annealing.
A post-processing anneal below recrystallization can relax residual stress while otherwise preserving the relevant microstructure.
Residual thermal stresses pre-stress the HfNbTaTiZr microstructure.
Residual stresses modify dislocation mobility.
Interfacial mismatch and precipitate structure can affect elevated-temperature creep behavior.
Heterogeneous matrices and coherent nanoprecipitates can govern alloy strength and deformation behavior.
Heterogeneous structures govern both strength and damping behavior in advanced alloys.
Residual thermal stresses are the common cause of the alloy's tensile-creep, microhardness, and elastic-modulus anomalies.
Relative to annealed material, rapidly quenched HfNbTaTiZr will have higher yield strength.
Relative to annealed material, rapidly quenched HfNbTaTiZr will have greater high-temperature creep resistance.
Rapidly quenched HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit more pronounced elastic-modulus anomalies.
Stress-relieved samples will exhibit a more conventional stress–strain response and reduced creep resistance.
Stress-relieved samples will exhibit a more linear temperature dependence of elastic modulus.
The comparison will cover tensile and creep behavior from room temperature to 1250 °C and elastic modulus from 293 to 1100 K.
The comparison should include diffraction-based residual-stress measurements and microscopy to verify precipitate–matrix coherence.
The residual-stress hypothesis is falsified if verified stress relief produces no statistically significant change in stress–strain behavior, creep resistance, or thermoelastic response.
